Read the following text carefully and answer the given questions : On 30th September 2022, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised Repo Rate for the fourth time in a row. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decided to raise the policy rate by 50 basis points (1 basis point = 1/100th of a percent). After this announcement, the new repo rate stands at 5.9%, while the reverse repo rate continues to stand at 3.35%. Commercial banks borrow money from the Central Bank, when there is a shortage of funds. With the surge in the repo rate, borrowings by general public will become costlier, because as RBI hikes its repo rate it becomes costly for the banks to borrow short term funds from the Central Bank. As a result, the banks hike the rates at which customers borrow money from them, and the interest rate on retail loans is generally directly proportional to the repo rate. The increase of 0.50 percent in repo rate will lead to higher interest rates on loans for borrowers, so the Equated Monthly Instalments (EMIs) for repaying existing loans will also increase. questions.chapter: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal
questions.text: Read the following text carefully and answer the given questions : The stabilisation and structural adjustment measures, initiated under the 1991 “Economic Reforms” mark a watershed moment in India’s economic policies. For almost three decades since independence, India’s development strategy and economic policies were guided by the objectives of accelerating the growth of output and employment with social justice and equity. Ever since the 1970’s, it was realised that many of the regulations on economic activities had outlived their usefulness and were in fact hampering economic growth and development, so the government initiated milder liberalisation reforms for almost a decade since the early 1980’s. However, the Indian economy soon had to face the Gulf crisis, leading to uncertainties about oil prices, external payment problems, serious inflationary pressures, scarcities of essential commodities and deterioration of fiscal discipline — bringing the economy to the verge of an economic crisis. In response, the Government initiated stabilisation reforms (reduction in fiscal deficit, containment of growth in money supply, an exchange rate adjustment system) and structural adjustment measures (industrial delicensing, liberalisation of the policy regime governing international trade, deregulation of the financial sector). (a) Briefly outline any two reasons for the initiation of Economic Reforms in 1991. (b) Government introduced a set of stabilisation and structural reforms to solve the economic crisis. State the key initiatives and objectives of these policies adopted by the Government of India.
